Idempotency is a stronger property that applies to the application of an event to state, not the act of appending the event itself. The log preserves the total order of appends, and as long as retried appends do not corrupt the log (i.e., they are safe), deterministic replay is achieved by the consumer applying idempotent logic or sequence-based deduplication to the stream.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a safe operation appends events with distinct, randomly generated contents upon retry (e.g., different timestamps or UUIDs), the log will contain divergent events, breaking deterministic replay regardless of consumer logic.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A writer appending an event to a log might safely append duplicates if the log assigns an append position and a producer ID, allowing downstream consumers to deterministically ignore duplicates during replay. The writer's job is just to persist the event safely.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
